_comment: Comment corpus for warming. Used by warm skills when planning a 'comment' action against another user's post. Skills read this; you edit it. The committed default carries only universal phrases that work across most domains. For brand-specific phrase sets (faith / dev / lifestyle / etc.) see personal.example/comment-corpus.brand.json.

_authoring_rules.no_terminal_punctuation: skip periods/exclamation marks — they read formal/bot. Apostrophes inside words are fine (don't / he's).
_authoring_rules.no_self_promo: never reference your own brand / app / URL in a comment — that's spam, gets you flagged
_authoring_rules.voice: casual social-native, brief enough that repetition isn't immediately obvious

_usage.selection: Skills sample one phrase per planned comment action. Default category is 'universal'. Future: detect target-post theme and pick from the matching category.
anti_pattern_safeguards: Do NOT use the same phrase twice within 7 days against the same platform.
Do NOT comment on the same author within 30 days.
Do NOT comment + like + save on the same post in one pass — pick at most ONE engagement per target post.
Skip any candidate whose author handle matches your brand's exclude_handles_substring list (set in config/brand.json).

Skip any target whose visible text matches a reply-prompt pattern: /reply with/i, /comment .{1,15} below/i, /type ["']?[A-Za-z]{2,12}["']?/i, /say .{1,20} below/i. These posts expect a specific keyword and a generic corpus phrase will look obviously off.
Lean on captions/alt-text for image-based prompts when available — a fully-image-driven prompt won't surface in tweetText. If alt-text isn't accessible, prefer to skip rather than guess.
_usage.track_used: When a comment is posted, append the phrase + platform + target post id + timestamp to ~/.social-skills/state/comment-history.json so the de-dup checks above can run.
